ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level ratio; predominantly high-intensity white pixels (approx. 85%) on the central ventral surface, contrasted against low-intensity black pixels along the peripheral edges and the insertion point.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white region occupying the central and medial fluke surface. Solid black pigmentation band along the entire trailing edge. A series of dark, finger-like projections extend from the peduncle into the white field at the fluke base. A single distinct vertical dark mark is located on the medial inner left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 35-40 degrees; vertex is well-defined and centered.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serrations (jagged peaks and valleys) extracted along the continuous linear boundary of the trailing edge, clearly silhouetted against the background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curve fitted to the trailing edges of both lobes, sweeping outward and terminating in sharp, slightly upward-tilted distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-contrast pixel clusters (dark on white and light on dark) localized at the extreme distal tips of both lobes; smaller dark clusters visible near the median notch.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A distinct, unaligned vertical dark linear mark is detected on the inner left lobe; faint horizontal scratches are visible on the right lobe surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Heavy irregular scarring and tissue erosion at the distal tips consistent with parasitic colonization or mechanical wear; non-uniform trailing edge topography indicating cumulative physical trauma.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'comb-like' black pigmentation pattern at the peduncle insertion point extending roughly 15% into the total fluke depth.
